chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil ibn Dirraj from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If a man divorces a woman, and she marries another, and he divorces her, and she marries the first man again, and he divorces her, and she marries another man, and he divorces her, and she marries the first man again, then if he divorces her for the third time in this manner, she does not become permissible to him ever."

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever has sexual intercourse with his paternal aunt or his maternal aunt, their two daughters are forbidden to him, and they do not become permissible to him by marriage ever.
That was narrated - Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to me from Abu Ayyub from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Muhammad ibn Muslim asked him (the Imam) while I was sitting, about a man who had sexual intercourse with his maternal aunt while he was young, then restrained himself: Can he marry her daughter? He said: "No."
He said: Indeed, he had not fully penetrated her; it was something less than that. He said: "He lied."
And whoever marries a young girl and consummates the marriage with her before she reaches nine years of age, they are separated, and she does not become permissible to him ever.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions under which a woman becomes permanently forbidden to her first husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between permanent (mu'abbad) and temporary prohibitions in Shia jurisprudence, specifically addressing the 'three divorces' rule where a woman becomes permanently forbidden to her first husband after marrying and being divorced by two other men. It further establishes that sexual intercourse (even if not full penetration) with a paternal or maternal aunt creates a permanent prohibition for her daughters, while consummation with a girl under nine years of age results in permanent separation. These rulings highlight the significance of actual consummation in establishing permanent marital bonds and prohibitions.
